documents.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence Statement
documents.stance_why: The statement sets no ban or default itself: use "will follow existing University policies and procedures", unauthorized use goes to Academic Conduct Procedures, and students are told to "ask your instructors for clarification", which leaves what is authorized to instructors.
documents.summary: A short Academic Affairs statement saying AI use must follow existing university policies. Students stay responsible for AI-based submissions, must document AI use, and face Academic Conduct Procedures for unauthorized use. It points them to instructors when unsure.

units.why: Opening framing: AI is "a tool for innovative research and discovery across disciplines", the university's own view, so informs; P56 (institution-level principle) fits, not P44, which concerns teaching professional skills.
units.anchor: considers artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool for innovative research and discovery across disciplines
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on span, modality, type and phase. Actor differed (A admin, B all) and so did unit_stance (A encourage, B permit) and topics. The source sentence is the university stating its own view and addresses no one, so admin is the speaker-side actor. It calls AI a useful research tool but recommends nothing, so permit is the least strengthened reading. Topics reduced to governance, since the sentence is institutional framing.

units.why: "Use of generative AI tools by any member of the LIU community will follow existing University policies and procedures" binds everyone and sets the scope and framework; P56 fits as an institution-wide framework.
units.anchor: generative AI tools by any member of the LIU community will follow existing University policies
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on all codes (P56, all, general, must). Topics differed (A governance, B default-stance); the sentence subordinates AI use to existing policy, which is governance, so A's topics kept.

units.why: 'You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query' makes students accountable for submissions; P29 fits as the general accountability rule. The two parenthetical examples are coded separately as P52 and P31.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query
units.resolution_why: Both coders coded P29 with the same codes. B folded the parenthetical examples into one long normalized policy; A kept the anchor alone and coded the two examples separately. The anchor alone states the accountability rule, so policy is null and the examples are separate units.

units.why: The parenthetical "does not violate intellectual property laws" asks students to ensure submitted AI content respects IP, P52 (copyright).
units.anchor: does not violate intellectual property laws
units.policy: Students ensure that information they submit based on an AI query does not violate intellectual property laws
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. Source: the parenthetical says students are responsible that the information 'does not violate intellectual property laws'. This is a concrete requirement distinct from general accountability, so it is kept as P52. B captured it only inside its P29 policy text and topics.

units.why: "or contain misinformation or unethical content" requires students to ensure AI-based submissions are accurate and ethical; P31 (verify output) fits best since it concerns misinformation.
units.policy: Students ensure that information they submit based on an AI query does not contain misinformation or unethical content
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. Source: the same parenthetical adds that the information must not 'contain misinformation or unethical content'. Kept as a distinct requirement; P31 fits the misinformation concern. B did not code it separately.

units.why: "Your use of AI tools must be properly documented in accordance with university policies on academic honesty" requires documentation of AI use, P24 (disclose); no tool/prompt details so not P25.
units.anchor: must be properly documented in accordance with university policies on academic honesty
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on all codes (P24, student, during-work, must, permit).

units.why: "found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways will be subject to LIU's Academic Conduct Procedures" classes unauthorized use as misconduct handled by integrity process, P36.
units.anchor: used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways will be subject to LIU’s Academic Conduct Procedures
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P36, when-misuse and informs. Policy text differed (A null, B normalized restatement) and unit_stance differed (A prohibit, B restrict). The source says only that unauthorized use is subject to Academic Conduct Procedures, so the anchor alone states the rule (policy null). Because the passage bans only unauthorized use, restrict fits, not prohibit.

units.why: "When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask your instructors for clarification" tells unsure students to ask, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask your instructors for clarification
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on all codes (P10, student, course-start, should).

notes: Single thin university-level document (about 1,000 characters). No school, computing or course documents found. Reconciled from two coders; see resolution_why on each unit.
